prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a gym scene from a top-down egocentric viewpoint where the camera wearer stands holding two dumbbells at 0.3–0.6 m in the bottom foreground, while another person lies back on an exercise bench in front and below them at roughly 1.0–1.5 m, flanked by a stationary bike on the left (1.2–1.8 m, separated from the bench by ~0.8 m) and floor bags on the right (~1.5 m). Across the five frames, the camera wearer steps closer and tilts their view upward while the reclining person leans back onto the bench, bringing the reclined person's upper body and upward-facing head (which looks toward the camera wearer in frames 4–5) into view as the wearer's extended arms bring the dumbbells within 0.2–0.4 m (arm's reach) of both individuals' hands by frame 5. In frames 1–3, the reclining person's upper torso and head are cropped out of the top of the frame, and in frames 4–5 the camera wearer's extended arms and dumbbells partially occlude the reclining person's legs and lower torso. Compared to RGB alone, the depth gradient clearly separates the elevated foreground arms and dumbbells (bright white) from the dark floor and the mid-gray reclining figure directly beneath them. However, the depth map is unreliable around thin and dark structures, blurring the stationary bike frame into the floor, merging the bench pads with the person's dark leggings, and bleeding bright depth values between the dumbbells and the reclining person's body in frame 5.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates two people in the scene: the camera wearer's lower body and outstretched arms at the bottom (0.3–0.8 m from the viewpoint) and the second person reclining on the bench in front and below them (1.0–1.5 m away, closing to ~0.5 m from the wearer's hands by frame 5). As the camera wearer steps forward and tilts the camera across frames 1 to 5, the reclining person's mask expands from only knees and thighs cropped at the top edge (frames 1–2) to their full torso, outstretched arms, and upward-facing head looking toward the camera wearer (frames 4–5), with both individuals' hands and the held dumbbells coming within arm's reach of each other. In frames 4 and 5, the camera wearer's arms and dumbbells overlap and partially occlude the lower body of the reclining person. The map provides clean 2D silhouette boundaries for the two people against the dark gym floor and equipment that have low contrast in RGB. However, it is unreliable in object classification and consistency: it completely misses the exercise bench, stationary bike, right-side bags, and right-hand dumbbell, mislabels the left dumbbell as a 'cell phone' in frame 1, swaps the reclining person's mask colour from cyan to pink after frame 1, and merges the camera wearer's arms and dumbbells into the reclining person's mask in frame 4 and on the right side of frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the 2D skeletal keypoints of the reclining person in front of and below the camera wearer (~1.0–1.5 m away) and the camera wearer's hands in the bottom foreground (~0.4–0.6 m away), while leaving background gym equipment (bike on the left, bench beneath, bags on the right) unrepresented. Across frames 1 to 5, as the camera wearer approaches and looks further up the bench, the reclining person's skeleton enters the view: completely absent in frames 1–2 when their upper body is out of frame, appearing as a partial torso and left hand in frame 3, and revealing a supine torso with spread arms and facial keypoints oriented upward toward the camera wearer in frames 4–5. In frame 4, two magenta hand skeletons at the bottom show the camera wearer's hands holding dumbbells within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m) of the reclining person's hips and outstretched hands, and in frame 5 the wearer's left hand approaches the reclining person's right hand while the wearer's arms partially occlude the person's legs. Compared to the RGB strip, the pose map explicitly localizes joint articulations, torso orientation, and finger positions even where blue shirt fabric and dark leggings blend into the background. However, the map is unreliable when bodies are heavily cropped or occluded: it fails to detect either person in frames 1–2, produces a distorted torso with a missing right hand and misaligned legs in frame 3, omits the camera wearer's right hand and merges their left hand into the reclining person's right wrist in frame 5, and misses the reclining person's left hand keypoints in frame 5.
